## When Federal Policy Shifts, Local Systems Absorb the Shock {.text-slide .shock-slide}

## Core Question {.text-slide}

Where are high-need neighborhoods served by relatively thin pantry infrastructure?

- This is a planning tool for outreach and referral targeting.

> In St. Louis, nearby pantry presence does not consistently align with the share of residents reporting food insecurity.

## How We Identify Service Gaps {.text-slide .measure-slide}

We combine neighborhood food insecurity estimates with pantry proximity to flag service gaps.

```{=html}
<div class="measure-claim">We are mapping gaps in the support system, not poverty.</div>

<div class="measure-flow">
  <span>Food Insecurity</span>
  <span class="measure-op">+</span>
  <span>Pantry Access</span>
  <img class="measure-arrow" src="visuals/icon-arrow-right.svg" alt="" aria-hidden="true">
  <span>Service Gap Signal</span>
</div>

<div class="method-grid">
  <div class="method-card">
    <img class="method-icon" src="visuals/icon-need.svg" alt="">
    <div class="method-title">Food insecurity</div>
    <div class="method-text">CDC tract estimates of food insecurity.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="method-card">
    <img class="method-icon" src="visuals/icon-access.svg" alt="">
    <div class="method-title">Pantry access</div>
    <div class="method-text">Pantries within ~1 mile of each tract.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="method-card">
    <img class="method-icon" src="visuals/icon-index.svg" alt="">
    <div class="method-title">Combined signal (FPDI)</div>
    <div class="method-text">High need plus thin nearby coverage.</div>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="measure-guardrails">
  <div><strong>What this map does:</strong> Identifies mismatches between neighborhood need and nearby pantry coverage.</div>
  <div><strong>What this map does not do:</strong> It is not a poverty map or a measure of individual hardship.</div>
</div>

<div class="measure-sources">Sources: CDC PLACES (2023); St. Louis Area Foodbank pantry locations; Census tract geography.</div>
```

<details open>
<summary>Q&A details: data provenance and construction</summary>

- Regional data assembly uses the St. Louis Dashboard infrastructure developed at WashU.
- Food insecurity is the CDC PLACES 2023 tract estimate based on adults reporting food did not last and they lacked money to buy more in the past 12 months.
- Pantry locations come from the St. Louis Area Foodbank pantry locator and were geocoded for tract-level analysis.

</details>

## How We Build The FPDI {.text-slide}

1. Estimate pantry presence within about 1 mile of each tract centroid.
2. Measure tract-level food insecurity prevalence.
3. Standardize both measures and scale to **0-100**.

Higher values indicate higher need relative to nearby pantry presence.

<details open>
<summary>Q&A details: interpretation of low and high values</summary>

- FPDI is scaled 0-100: higher values indicate larger unmet need relative to nearby pantry presence.
- Low values can reflect either: 1) low food insecurity and limited pantry presence, or 2) high need with relatively dense nearby pantry coverage.
- Pantry coverage is currently proxied as access within ~1 mile because reliable capacity/hours/catchment data are not consistently available.

</details>

## How To Read The Maps {.text-slide}

- **Step 1:** Where need is high.
- **Step 2:** Where pantries are concentrated.
- **Step 3:** Where the two are poorly aligned.

Read sequentially: need -> pantry presence -> combined index.

## Need and Access Are Weakly Aligned {.chart-slide}

Need and pantry access are only weakly aligned across tracts.

```{r}
#| fig-width: 10.0
#| fig-height: 4.6
#| fig-align: center
suppressPackageStartupMessages({
  library(dplyr)
  library(ggplot2)
  library(readr)
  library(scales)
  library(sf)
  library(stringr)
})

normalize_geoid <- function(x) stringr::str_pad(as.character(x), width = 11, side = "left", pad = "0")

fi_raw <- readr::read_csv("../food_insecurity.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
fd_raw <- readr::read_csv("../food_pantry_desert.csv", show_col_types = FALSE)
tract <- sf::st_read("../output/stl_food_access_tracts_reporting.gpkg", quiet = TRUE)

fi <- fi_raw %>%
  transmute(GEOID = normalize_geoid(GEOID), prevalence_pct = as.numeric(.data[[names(fi_raw)[2]]]))

fd <- fd_raw %>%
  transmute(GEOID = normalize_geoid(GEOID), desert_raw = as.numeric(.data[[names(fd_raw)[2]]]))

tract_access <- tract %>%
  mutate(GEOID = normalize_geoid(GEOID)) %>%
  filter(grepl("St\\. Louis city|St\\. Louis County", NAME)) %>%
  st_drop_geometry() %>%
  transmute(GEOID, pantries_within_1mi = as.numeric(n_pantries_nearby))

scatter_df <- fi %>%
  inner_join(fd, by = "GEOID") %>%
  left_join(tract_access, by = "GEOID") %>%
  mutate(
    fpdi_0_100 = scales::rescale(desert_raw, to = c(0, 100), na.rm = TRUE),
    pantries_within_1mi = ifelse(is.na(pantries_within_1mi), 0, pantries_within_1mi),
    access_group = ifelse(pantries_within_1mi == 0, "0 pantries", "1+ pantries"),
    access_size = ifelse(pantries_within_1mi == 0, 1, pantries_within_1mi)
  ) %>%
  filter(!is.na(prevalence_pct), !is.na(fpdi_0_100))

rho <- suppressWarnings(cor(
  scatter_df$prevalence_pct,
  scatter_df$fpdi_0_100,
  method = "spearman",
  use = "complete.obs"
))

ggplot(scatter_df, aes(x = prevalence_pct, y = fpdi_0_100, color = access_group, size = access_size)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.72, stroke = 0.15) +
  geom_smooth(
    aes(x = prevalence_pct, y = fpdi_0_100),
    method = "lm",
    formula = y ~ x,
    se = TRUE,
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "#1f2937",
    fill = "#cbd5e1",
    linewidth = 0.9
  ) +
  scale_color_manual(
    name = "Tract type",
    values = c("0 pantries" = "#205732", "1+ pantries" = "#971B2F")
  ) +
  scale_size_area(
    name = "Pantries within 1 mile",
    max_size = 6,
    breaks = c(1, 2, 5, 10, 15),
    labels = c("0 or 1", "2", "5", "10", "15")
  ) +
  scale_x_continuous(
    name = "Food insecurity (% of adults)",
    breaks = scales::pretty_breaks(6),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.04))
  ) +
  scale_y_continuous(
    name = "Food Pantry Desert Index (0-100)",
    limits = c(0, 100),
    breaks = seq(0, 100, 20),
    expand = expansion(mult = c(0.02, 0.04))
  ) +
  labs(
    subtitle = paste0("Spearman correlation (need vs FPDI): ", format(round(rho, 2), nsmall = 2)),
    caption = "Each point is one census tract in St. Louis City or St. Louis County. Green points indicate tracts with 0 pantries within 1 mile."
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_family = "Avenir Next") +
  theme(
    panel.grid.minor = element_blank(),
    panel.grid.major = element_line(color = "#e5e7eb", linewidth = 0.4),
    axis.title = element_text(size = 12, color = "#1f2937"),
    axis.text = element_text(size = 10, color = "#374151"),
    plot.subtitle = element_text(size = 10.5, color = "#475569"),
    plot.caption = element_text(size = 8.5, color = "#6b7280"),
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.title = element_text(size = 9.5),
    legend.text = element_text(size = 8.5),
    legend.box.spacing = grid::unit(0.25, "lines")
  ) +
  guides(
    color = guide_legend(order = 1, override.aes = list(size = 3.5, alpha = 0.9)),
    size = guide_legend(order = 2, nrow = 1)
  )
```

## Limits To Keep In Mind {.text-slide}

- Proximity does not capture pantry capacity, hours, or eligibility.
- Pantry location data may be incomplete.
- This is a planning tool, not an individual diagnostic instrument.

<details open>
<summary>Q&A details: concrete example of measurement error risk</summary>

- Some pantries serve wider catchment areas than a one-mile radius; for example, district-based service models can make local unmet-need estimates appear higher than operational reality in specific tracts.
- This is why FPDI should be validated with provider and community knowledge before targeting decisions.

</details>

## What This Enables In Practice {.text-slide .enable-slide}

Use FPDI as a shared planning layer for triage, local validation, and partner coordination.

```{=html}
<div class="takeaway-grid">
  <div class="takeaway-card">
    <img class="takeaway-icon" src="visuals/icon-index.svg" alt="">
    <div class="takeaway-title">Prioritize</div>
    <div class="takeaway-text">Identify outreach-priority tracts for proactive screening and referral.</div>
    <div class="takeaway-meta"><strong>Output:</strong> tract priority list for weekly outreach planning.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="takeaway-card">
    <img class="takeaway-icon" src="visuals/icon-access.svg" alt="">
    <div class="takeaway-title">Validate</div>
    <div class="takeaway-text">Pair index signals with local provider and community knowledge.</div>
    <div class="takeaway-meta"><strong>Output:</strong> vetted hotspot list with provider notes on hours, catchment, and constraints.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="takeaway-card">
    <img class="takeaway-icon" src="visuals/icon-need.svg" alt="">
    <div class="takeaway-title">Coordinate</div>
    <div class="takeaway-text">Use a common geographic framework across clinics and partners.</div>
    <div class="takeaway-meta"><strong>Output:</strong> shared cross-agency targeting map for referrals and resource deployment.</div>
  </div>
</div>

<div class="enable-note">Intended use: coordination and service routing at neighborhood scale, not individual-level diagnosis.</div>
```

## Next Steps {.text-slide .next-slide}

Move from a static indicator to an operational planning tool used across partner organizations.

```{=html}

  </div>
  <div class="next-card">
    <div class="next-title">2. Add Time-Sensitive Access</div>
    <div class="next-text">Integrate mobile pantry schedules and temporal variation in service availability.</div>
    <div class="next-meta"><strong>Deliverable:</strong> monthly and seasonal gap maps.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="next-card">
    <div class="next-title">3. Connect Referrals to Outcomes</div>
    <div class="next-text">Link clinic screening/referral workflows with follow-up outcomes at neighborhood scale.</div>
    <div class="next-meta"><strong>Deliverable:</strong> closed-loop referral performance metrics.</div>
  </div>
  <div class="next-card">
    <div class="next-title">4. Deploy a Partner Dashboard</div>
    <div class="next-text">Publish a shared, updateable map layer for clinics, providers, and coordinators.</div>

  </div>
</div>
<div class="next-note">Recommended sequencing: supply realism -> time-sensitive access -> referral integration -> live dashboard operations.</div>
```
